support: Say what you like about {head}, the {power} has never run smoother.
The {party} understands people like me. I'd vote for them twice if I could.
{head} is the only {title} in living memory worth the chair.
Things are finally moving in the right direction under the {party}.
My grandparents would be proud of what the {power} is becoming.
I put a {party} pin on my coat and I wear it everywhere.
Whatever the grumblers say, {head} inherited a mess and is cleaning it up.
Strong leadership, steady hands. That's all I ask, and that's what we have.
oppose: Don't get me started on {head}. Worst {title} the {power} has ever suffered.
The {party} bought this government and now we're all paying the interest.
Every promise {head} made has quietly evaporated. Typical.
The {power} deserves better than this circus they call a government.
One more term of the {party} and there'll be nothing left to govern.
I didn't vote for this, and I know plenty who say the same.
They call it order. I call it a boot on our necks.
Someone ought to ask {head} where all the money actually went.
apathetic: Politics? I have enough trouble keeping bread on the table.
{title} this, {election} that... none of it changes my rent.
They're all the same once they're in the chair, if you ask me.
I stopped reading the proclamations years ago. Better for the digestion.
Whoever wins, I'll still be up at dawn doing the same work.
My neighbor won't shut up about the {party}. I just nod and think about lunch.
radical: Talk changes nothing. The {power} needs fire, not another {election}.
When the time comes, everyone will have to pick a side. I've picked mine.
The {party} is the only thing standing between us and the abyss, history will vindicate us.
They laughed at us in the squares. They won't laugh forever.
Every empire looks eternal the week before it falls.
I keep a list of everyone who said it couldn't be done.

upcoming: Only {days} days until the {election}. You can feel it in the streets.
The {election} is {days} days off and the candidates are already at each other's throats.
{days} days left. I haven't decided, and don't you dare try to convince me.
They've started painting slogans on the walls again, {election} season.
Everyone smiles more before a {election}. It never lasts.
I'm told the {election} is in {days} days. The bunting is already up.
won: My side actually won the last {election}. I'm still not used to it.
I voted for {winner} and for once it counted for something.
We won! Now let's see if they remember us little people.
There was dancing in our street the night {winner} took it.
I keep the victory broadsheet folded in my coat pocket.
lost: {winner} won. I still can't believe people fell for it.
My vote went straight into the gutter, as usual.
The {election} was decided before a single vote, mark my words.
We'll be back. Losing one {election} isn't losing the argument.
I don't talk politics with my cousin anymore. Not since {winner} won.

rumor: They say {rumorSubject} is mixed up in some {rumorKind}. I heard it from three people.
Have you heard about {rumorSubject}? Something about a {rumorKind}. Hush-hush.
Everyone at the market is whispering about {rumorSubject} and that {rumorKind} business.
I don't spread gossip... but {rumorSubject}? A {rumorKind}? Where there's smoke...
My barber swears the {rumorSubject} {rumorKind} story is true. Barbers know things.
If even half of what they say about {rumorSubject} is true, heads will roll.
grumble: Between you and me, {gripe} is bleeding us dry.
I could live with everything else if it weren't for {gripe}.
They expect us to smile and thank them for {gripe}. Unbelievable.
My father never had to put up with anything like {gripe}.
First it was temporary, now {gripe} is just... life.
Someone in the capital got promoted for inventing {gripe}, I guarantee it.
officeHolder: Being {office} of {group} is mostly paperwork and complaints. Mostly complaints.
They call me {office} now. My mother finally tells the neighbors about me.
Everyone wants a favor from the {office}. Few remember the {office} at festival time.
I never wanted to be {office}, but somebody competent had to do it.

lines: Did you follow the last election? A disgrace.
You say that every time your side loses.
My side? I vote on principle, not habit!
Funny how your principles always pick the same color.
Taxes again. The capital eats and we starve.
Roads, guards, festivals, you think those are free?
I've seen our road. I want my money back.
Then run for office and fix it yourself!
The hyperpowers carve up the map like a roast.
Better a strong patron than chaos on the border.
Until the patron decides your town is the price.
That's why you pick the winning patron.
Whoever wins these elections, the bread costs more.
Politicians change. The queue at the bakery is forever.
Maybe the baker should run things for a while.
She'd have my vote. At least she rises early.
